newsitem.title: UK: European bonds break through key support levels.
newsitem.headline: European bonds break through key support levels.

text.p: European bonds look shaky after tumbling through several defences on Monday, dealers said.
"Sentiment is very negative," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank in London.
"Everything is breaking down through key support levels."
June Bund futures fell below a 101.16 retracement level earlier in the session, and then through 100.88, the high on January 22.
They were trading at 100.60 at 1520 GMT, down 83 basis points from Friday's close and slightly firmer than a session low of 100.59.

Talk that Europe's single currency project might be delayed grew on Monday after German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's weekend remarks that meeting the economic targets for membership took precedence over the timetable.
But dealers said specific remarks about Europe were less important than the technical market picture.
"We are very oversold -- we should be buying it from here," said Beauchamp.
Other European bonds took their lead from Bunds. June French bond futures dropped to 128.30 before inching up to 128.36, 94 basis points down on Friday's close.
Prime Minister John Major's announcement of a May 1 British election was merely a sideshow to the more important issues of Europe, dealers said.
"We've got far more problems with EMU than we have with a Labour government," one French broker at LIFFE said.
Britain's opposition Labour party is widely expected to win the UK election, and enjoys around a 20 point lead in polls.
Gilts fell to 110-16, off an earlier low of 110-04, and 21/32 below the prior close.

Italian bonds were hardest hit, falling to a low of 124.22 before making some headway to 124.39, 1.27 down on Friday's close. European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) divergence trades were causing peripheral European markets to underperform, dealers said.
